featured_techniques.technique: Diagnosing a door lock actuator by observing lock travel with the key fob and door button
Door panel removal to access the locking mechanism and actuator
Cable movement testing by manipulating cables with the door panel removed
Disassembly and inspection of the internal locking actuator
Off-vehicle functional test of actuator to demonstrate operation
Replacement planning and directing viewers to a dedicated replacement video

locations.basis: Transcript explicitly states the vehicle model and work occurs on the door panel inside the door
locations.name: Door panel (inside the door) of a 2014 Subaru Forester

concepts: Model: 2014 Subaru Forester
Door lock on this door does not fully lock when activated
Other doors lock normally; audible noise and partial movement observed
sections.description: The presenter notes a single door acting up, with incomplete lock movement and an audible cue, setting up the goal to diagnose the cause.
sections.title: Symptom identification on the target door

concepts: Key fob/lock button tested outside the vehicle
Lock moves a little but does not reach the locked position
Signs of possible binding or internal interference prompting door-panel diagnosis
sections.description: Using the door lock button from outside, the lock advances only slightly, accompanied by an inside-door audible sound, indicating the issue may be internal to the door mechanism.
sections.title: External lock test and initial diagnosis logic

concepts: Door panel removed
Cables exposed in the hand
Key used to test cable movement
sections.description: The panel is removed to gain access to the locking cable and actuator, enabling direct observation of the cable behavior during lock/unlock attempts.
sections.title: Door panel removal and access to locking components

concepts: Observation: white cable to the locking unit shows binding
Inference: binding likely responsible for inability to fully lock
sections.description: Visual cue of binding in the locking cable pathway suggests the fault lies at or beyond the cable connection to the locking unit.
sections.title: Identification of binding in the locking cable

concepts: Locking unit removed from the vehicle
Attempted disassembly with hand tools
Humorous note about using a hammer vs. screwdriver
sections.description: The actuator assembly is taken apart to inspect its internals, with the presenter outlining the intent to reveal what operates inside the unit.
sections.title: Disassembly and internal inspection begins

concepts: Reconnect wiring harness
Lock and unlock actions tested on the removed/partially assembled unit
Explanation of how pushing the signal drives the motor, which pulls the cable to operate the lock
sections.description: With the assembly tested outside the door, the presenter demonstrates how the actuator translates motor motion into cable movement that locks or unlocks the door.
sections.title: Functional testing of the isolated actuator assembly

concepts: Inside-the-door mechanism demonstrated
Decision to replace the faulty component rather than reassemble a partial unit
Direct viewers to the replacement video on 1A Auto
sections.description: The host confirms the fault and opts for replacement, inviting viewers to consult their replacement guide for the actual installation.
sections.title: Conclusion and replacement plan

summary: This tutorial-clip from 1A Auto demonstrates diagnosing a sticking door lock actuator on a 2014 Subaru Forester. The host first confirms that the lock on one door only moves a short distance and produces an audible cue, then systematically tests the mechanism by inspecting the cables and opening the door panel to access the lock actuator. He identifies binding in the locking cable, disassembles the actuator to inspect internal components, and demonstrates how the lock motor translates rotation into cable motion. The video concludes with a plan to replace the faulty unit and a note that viewers can watch 1A Auto’s replacement video for the actual part install.
title: Diagnosing and Replacing a Faulty Door Lock Actuator on a 2014 Subaru Forester
